rfm_tuples.R: The allowance for credit losses was 224.73% of nonperforming loans at December 31, 2024 as compared to 302.05% at December 31, 2023 ... The decline in the coverage of the allowance to nonperforming and nonaccrual loans from December 31, 2023 to December 31, 2024 largely relates to one nonperforming relationship with an amortized cost basis of $14.0 million that is individually evaluated for purposes of the allowance for credit losses which had no reserve established at December 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: a $14M individually-evaluated nonperforming loan with ZERO reserve implies management believes collateral fully covers the exposure. Verify whether the Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09) maintains the zero-reserve treatment or quietly charges off / reserves up, and whether ACL coverage stabilizes or further deteriorates.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q discloses ACL coverage rose to 245.33% of nonperforming loans (vs 224.73% at 12/31/24) and 260.99% of nonaccrual (vs 253.17%). Total nonperforming assets ticked up to $48.0M at 3/31/25. Q1 CECL forecast weighting shifted from 80%/20% baseline/downside (12/31/24) BACK to 75%/25% (3/31/25), partially reversing the 2024 reduction (which had moved from 70/30 -> 80/20). No charge-off disclosed against the $14M relationship. The directional improvement in coverage and the reversion to more conservative CECL weighting is mildly reassuring.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B is satisfied: the implied claim ('zero reserve is appropriate because collateral covers it') is at least not contradicted within 90 days. Q1 2025 actually showed coverage IMPROVING and CECL weights re-tightening (75/25), suggesting management is not optimistically managing-to-target.

rfm_tuples.R: At December 31, 2024, the weightings were 80% and 20% for the baseline and downside economic forecasts, respectively ... These increases to the allowance for credit losses were partially offset by a change in forecast scenario weightings from 70% baseline and 30% downside to 80% baseline and 20% downside.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: detect 'reserve-friendly' CECL assumption drift. Management EXPLICITLY disclosed that shifting from 70/30 -> 80/20 (more optimistic baseline) released reserves. Verify (a) magnitude of reserve release attributable to the weighting shift, and (b) whether the Q1 10-Q reverses this.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K sensitivity disclosure: 10% increase to downside (i.e., reversing back to 70/30) -> 4% increase in overall ACL; 100% downside -> 33% ACL increase. On a $114.4M January 1 ACL base, the 70->80 baseline shift implies roughly $4-5M of reserve release in 2024. Q1 2025 10-Q reset the weighting back to 75/25 (acknowledged in MD&A), partially reversing the 2024 release within one quarter.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: management's 2024 ACL benefit was partially driven by a more-optimistic CECL assumption shift, not just improved underlying credit. Honesty offset: the assumption shift is EXPLICITLY disclosed (not hidden), and Q1 2025 already partially reverses it. Mild flag, not a red flag.

rfm_tuples.R: Within the CRE portfolio, approximately 81% comprises Non-Owner Occupied CRE, with the remaining 19% being Owner-Occupied CRE. Non-Owner Occupied CRE includes diverse sectors across the Company's markets such as residential rental properties (43%) and office spaces (18%), along with retail, manufacturing, mixed use, hotels and others. Notably, office CRE loans account for 6% of the total outstanding loans, predominantly serving suburban medical and professional tenants across suburban and small urban markets. These loans carry an average size of $1.9 million, with 9% maturing over the next two years.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: office CRE is the most-watched bank credit risk in 2024-25. Verify that the disclosed 6%-of-loans framing isn't hiding concentration in distressed CBD office, and that small-borrower granularity ($1.9M average) is consistent with disclosed total.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Office CRE 6% of total loans on disclosed ~$10B loan base implies ~$600M office portfolio. $1.9M average size implies ~316 distinct office loans, consistent with a granular suburban-medical/professional-tenant book. Only 9% maturing in next two years means refinancing wall is small (~$54M). 81% Non-Owner Occupied CRE concentration is meaningful but disclosed; only 18% of NOO CRE is office (rest is residential rental 43% + retail/manufacturing/etc).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: CRE office concentration is disclosed with sufficient granularity. Suburban medical/professional tenant mix is structurally less risky than CBD office. Refinancing wall is small. No hidden CRE-office concentration detected.

rfm_tuples.R: Total HTM securities amortized cost $842,921 [thousand] vs fair value $749,945 [thousand] (2024 year-end).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: derive the embedded HTM unrealized loss as a fraction of tangible common equity. AOCI excludes HTM losses for opt-out non-advanced approaches banks, so HTM losses are 'hidden' relative to regulatory capital.
rfm_tuples.M_value: HTM unrealized loss = $842.9M - $749.9M = $93.0M (~11% of amortized cost). Tangible common equity per the 10-K MD&A summary (tangible equity ratio 8.42% on assets ~ $13.9B) implies tangible common equity ~ $1.17B. Embedded HTM unrealized loss is therefore ~8% of TCE. 10-K does not 'hide' this -- it is disclosed in the securities table -- and it is materially smaller than the regional bank crisis-period exposures (SVB-era peers had 50-100%+ ratios). The figure also improved YoY (from $107M unrealized loss at 12/31/23 implied by $905M cost vs $814M FV).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: HTM AOCI-excluded losses are real but moderate (~8% of TCE) and improving. Disclosure is transparent (full table). No hidden duration-mismatch crisis.

rfm_tuples.R: Implicit claim: ordinary-course insider transactions through 2024. (10-K Form 4 ledger.)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: derive 'given a major M&A announcement, did insiders sell into the news?' Compare aggregate Form 4 'S'-coded shares sold (a) Jan-Aug 2024 baseline (pre-merger announcement), (b) Sep 9 - Dec 31 2024 (90-day post-announcement window), (c) Jan - May 14 2025 (post-announcement, pre-cutoff).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Aggregated transaction codes parsed from Form 4 XML for CIK 0000790359: Jan 1 - Sep 8 2024 (pre-announcement): 9,966 shares sold (S-coded) across 53 Form 4s, 120,183 shares acquired (A/P/M). Sep 9 - Dec 31 2024 (post-announcement 90-day window): 233,250 shares sold across 14 Form 4s, 0 shares acquired. Jan 1 - May 14 2025 (post-announcement, pre-cutoff): 5,000 shares sold across 29 Form 4s, 50,632 shares acquired. Named sellers Sep 13-Nov 25 2024 include Director V. Daniel Robinson II (150,000 shares Sept 13-17 across two days, prices $43.84-$44.79), Vice Chairman/Director John H. Watt Jr. (30,000 shares Oct-Nov), Director Jack H. Webb (10,000 shares Nov 25), Director Timothy E. Delaney (40,000 shares Nov 13).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B red flag (mild): aggregate insider sales rose ~23x (9,966 -> 233,250 shares) in the 90 days after merger announcement, then fell back to near zero in 2025. Robinson's 150K-share sale within 4-8 trading days of the Sept 9 announcement is the most striking single transaction. None of these are open-market purchase reversals; all are pure dispositions. Behavior is consistent with insiders monetizing into a merger-driven price strength rather than expressing confidence in the post-merger combined entity. This is disclosed via Form 4 but is not in the 10-K narrative, so it is a derived signal.

summary: NBT Bancorp is a stable upstate-NY community bank with multi-decade Big-4 audit tenure, no going-concern or material-weakness language, and an Evans Bancorp merger that closed on schedule (May 2, 2025) within the disclosed Q2 2025 window. Mode-A checks all PASS. The two mild Mode-B flags are (a) CECL forecast weightings shifted to a more optimistic 80/20 baseline/downside in 2024 (partially released reserves; Q1 2025 already reversed back to 75/25 -- honestly disclosed assumption drift), and (b) aggregate insider sales rose ~23x in the 90 days after the September 9, 2024 merger announcement (Director Robinson 150K shares within 8 days, plus three other directors), then collapsed back to near zero in 2025 -- consistent with monetizing into stock-price strength rather than confidence in the post-merger entity. Office CRE exposure is granular and suburban (6% of loans, $1.9M avg). HTM embedded losses are modest (~8% of TCE) and improving. No SHORT-tier disclosure concerns; the file reads as honest mid-sized regional bank with normal cyclical pressures.
